settings.alt: Mannequins in the embroidered dress of Kutchi communities, in a museum gallery
Gallery wall of framed embroidery panels beside costumed figures
A curved gallery of Kutchi costume under museum lighting
Figures in the ceremonial dress of twelve Kutchi communities, arranged in a circular gallery
settings.name: The Museum
settings.copy: Three galleries, a library and the crafts studios — the whole complex built around the collection.

settings.alt: A potter throwing a vessel on the wheel in the LLDC crafts studio
settings.name: Crafts Studio
settings.copy: A working space for craftspeople — weaving, block-printing, pottery and the metal work of Kutch.

settings.alt: An audience watching a craft film in the LLDC auditorium
settings.name: Auditorium
settings.copy: A 126-seater, fully equipped with audio-visual facilities.

settings.alt: A child block-printing cloth under an instructor’s hand
settings.name: Hands On Area
settings.copy: Inspired by the crafts? This is where you try them yourself.

settings.name: The Shop
settings.copy: Make sure you take back a little bit of Kutch with you.

settings.alt: The LLDC courtyard cafe at dusk, tables under a pergola
settings.name: The Cafe
settings.copy: Refresh yourself with a hot cup of masala chai.

settings.lines:
Ajrakhpur, on the Bhuj–Bhachau highway
State transport and private buses run there, as do shared chhakada-rickshaws
Bhuj itself: rail from Ahmedabad, Mumbai and Delhi, flights from Mumbai and Delhi
